title: Transported ordinary restriction evaluation and its mate equation
statement: For categories and adjunctions L ⊣ R, K ⊣ H and Lf ⊣ Rf, let F,G be the source/target system functors, ec,ed the finite evaluations, and S,T their finite models. Let p:G⋙ed≅T, q:F⋙ec≅S and μ:K⋙ed≅ec⋙Lf, ν:H⋙ec≅ed⋙Rf satisfy the evaluated counit equation Lf(ν_Z) εf = μ⁻¹_HZ ed(εsys_Z). Suppose r:L⋙G≅F⋙K and α:L⋙T≅S⋙Lf satisfy ed(r_M) μ_FM Lf(q_M)=p_LM α_M. Then evaluation of the right mate of r inverse, followed by ν and Rf(p), equals q followed by the right mate of α inverse. For the open coefficient equivalences of [def-sf-integral-open-operations], transportRestrictionEvaluation constructs ν naturally, whose component is exactly the counitRestrictionEvaluation word of the fixed equivalence units and counits.

source.place: Tags 03DJ and 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, ordinary quotient construction.

proof.text: Transport the slice restriction-evaluation isomorphism through the system and finite coefficient equivalences by their units and counits. Expand associators and whiskering to identify the component with the prescribed word.

Apply the finite adjunction Hom bijection inversely to the two sides. Naturality moves its counit past p. Substitute the evaluated system counit, move μ by naturality, and use the mate-counit equation. Naturality of p at the integral counit and the inverse of the r/α comparison equation leave the finite mate-counit word. Injectivity of the Hom bijection proves equality.

proof_origin.place: Ordinary mate calculation: naturality, equivalence triangles and the adjunction counit identities.

theorem evaluation_right_mate
    {A : Type a} {B : Type b} {C : Type c} {D : Type d}
    {P : Type e} {Q : Type f}
    [Category.{av} A] [Category.{bv} B] [Category.{cv} C] [Category.{dv} D]
    [Category.{ev} P] [Category.{fv} Q]
    {L : A ⥤ B} {R : B ⥤ A} {K : C ⥤ D} {H : D ⥤ C}
    {Lf : P ⥤ Q} {Rf : Q ⥤ P}
    (adj : L ⊣ R) (sys : K ⊣ H) (fin : Lf ⊣ Rf)
    (F : A ⥤ C) (G : B ⥤ D) (ec : C ⥤ P) (ed : D ⥤ Q)
    (S : A ⥤ P) (T : B ⥤ Q)
    (p : G ⋙ ed ≅ T) (q : F ⋙ ec ≅ S)
    (μ : K ⋙ ed ≅ ec ⋙ Lf) (ν : H ⋙ ec ≅ ed ⋙ Rf)
    (hε : ∀ Z : D, Lf.map (ν.hom.app Z) ≫ fin.counit.app (ed.obj Z) =
      μ.inv.app (H.obj Z) ≫ ed.map (sys.counit.app Z))
    (r : L ⋙ G ≅ F ⋙ K) (α : L ⋙ T ≅ S ⋙ Lf)
    (hr : ∀ M : A, ed.map (r.hom.app M) ≫ μ.hom.app (F.obj M) ≫
      Lf.map (q.hom.app M) = p.hom.app (L.obj M) ≫ α.hom.app M)
    (N : B) :
    ec.map ((mateEquiv adj sys (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ r.inv)).app N) ≫
        ν.hom.app (G.obj N) ≫ Rf.map (p.hom.app N) =
      q.hom.app (R.obj N) ≫
        (mateEquiv adj fin (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ α.inv)).app N
